findings.observation: Sheet 3 contains two electric notes sections: a labeled 'Electric Notes' section with five notes addressing tree pruning, easement access, erosion control, clearance maintenance, and relocation of facilities. A visual inspection of these notes and the 'Electric Transmission Notes' section below them confirms the absence of any disclaimer language indicating that the electric facilities shown are conceptual, preliminary in nature, not intended for bidding purposes, or subject to change by Austin Energy during final design. The Electric Notes section contains operational and safety requirements but does not include the required disclaimer statement.
findings.reasoning: The checklist item requires a note stating that 'electric facilities shown are conceptual only, should not be used for bidding purposes, and that final electric design by Austin Energy may vary from that shown and may require changes to site plan.' This disclaimer is necessary to set expectations about the preliminary nature of electric facilities and Austin Energy's final design authority. The absence of this disclaimer represents a deficiency in plan documentation. The notes present address operational requirements but do not provide the required conceptual/preliminary design disclaimer.
findings.comment: Austin Energy Notes section lacks required disclaimer stating that electric facilities are conceptual, preliminary in nature, not for bidding purposes, and subject to change during Austin Energy's final design review. Please add statement: 'Electric facilities shown are conceptual in nature and should not be used for bidding purposes. Final electric design by Austin Energy may vary from that shown and may require changes to the site plan.'

findings.observation: The 'Electric Notes' section on Sheet 3 contains five notes addressing tree work rights, easement access, erosion control, clearance maintenance, and facility relocation. No note is present requiring coordination with Austin Energy or notification to Austin Energy of changes that may affect electric requirements. The notes do not list the specific change types (building square footage, building location, detention facilities location, grading, spoil site locations) that require Austin Energy review.
findings.reasoning: AEDC 1.16.0 requires notification to Austin Energy when changes are proposed that may affect electric service requirements. This requirement protects both the applicant and Austin Energy by ensuring that significant site changes do not invalidate the preliminary electric design shown on plans. The grouping specifies that this note must identify specific change types including building square footage, building location, detention facilities, grading, and spoil sites. The absence of this coordination requirement note is a deficiency that could result in unapproved changes during construction.
findings.comment: Austin Energy Notes section must include a note requiring Austin Energy review of any changes affecting electric requirements. Please add statement: 'Austin Energy must review any changes to plans that may affect electric requirements, including changes in building square footage, building location, detention facilities location, grading, and spoil site locations.'

findings.observation: Sheet 3 contains two electric-related note sections. The first section heading reads 'Electric Notes' (not 'Austin Energy Notes'). The second section heading reads 'Electric Transmission Notes' (not 'Austin Energy Transmission Notes'). Neither section uses the required standard heading 'Austin Energy Notes.' A review of the General Site Plan Notes document requirements indicates the heading must use the exact text 'Austin Energy Notes' without variations such as 'Electric Notes,' 'Utility Notes,' 'City of Austin Electric Notes,' or similar.
findings.reasoning: The General Site Plan Notes document specifies required headings and warns that 'Changing the required text in your plan set will result in rejection of the application.' The heading 'Austin Energy Notes' is a standard, required element that helps contractors and developers identify the authority requiring the notes and ensures consistency with other project documentation. Using alternative headings such as 'Electric Notes' or 'Utility Notes' creates ambiguity about which utility the notes address. This is a formatting deficiency that affects plan clarity and compliance.
findings.comment: The section heading must read exactly 'Austin Energy Notes,' not 'Electric Notes' or other variations. Please change the section heading from 'Electric Notes' to 'Austin Energy Notes' on Sheet 3. Transmission-specific notes should be in a separate section headed 'Austin Energy Transmission Notes.'

findings.observation: Sheet 3 contains the Austin Energy notes twice: First, as a labeled 'Electric Notes' section with five notes (tree pruning, easement access, erosion control, clearance maintenance, relocation). Second, as an unheaded text block below the 'Electric Transmission Notes' section that contains identical content—five unnumbered paragraphs that are exact duplicates of the notes in the labeled section above. The duplicate block appears without a section heading and repeats notes already presented, creating redundancy on the same sheet.
findings.reasoning: Plan clarity and professional organization require that standard note sections appear once on a plan set. When the same notes appear multiple times on a single sheet, it creates confusion about which version is the controlling set of requirements and increases the likelihood of conflicting or inconsistent information during construction. The checklist specifically flags this as a reviewer convention deficiency. Duplicate sections should be consolidated into a single 'Austin Energy Notes' section to avoid ambiguity.
findings.comment: Austin Energy Notes section appears twice on Sheet 3 (as 'Electric Notes' and as a duplicate unheaded block). Please consolidate all notes into a single 'Austin Energy Notes' section and remove the duplicate unheaded block below the Transmission Notes section.

findings.observation: The Austin Energy notes on Sheet 3 include five notes addressing tree work, easement access, erosion control, clearance maintenance, and facility relocation. None of the notes present includes developer responsibility for designing and constructing conduit infrastructure or reference to the Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual. The grouping identifies that Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) shows electrical routing and infrastructure, indicating that conduit infrastructure is a component of this project. No note is present establishing developer responsibility for conduit design and construction per current Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual standards.
findings.reasoning: AEDC 1.3.0 establishes basic requirements for electric distribution service, including developer-installed conduit when applicable. The required note must establish that: (1) the developer is responsible for designing and constructing conduit to meet current Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual standards, (2) the developer may be responsible for conductor installation if it is determined during design that developer funding is appropriate, (3) the developer must coordinate with other utilities to resolve conflicts, and (4) all costs are the applicant's responsibility. The current reference to 'Design Criteria Manual' (not outdated standards) is essential. Absence of this note creates ambiguity about developer responsibilities during construction.
findings.comment: Austin Energy Notes section must include a note establishing developer responsibility for conduit design and installation. Please add: 'Developer is responsible for designing and constructing all conduit and related infrastructure to meet current Austin Energy Design Criteria Manual, including installation of conductors if determined during design (prior to building permit issuance) that developer will fund conductor installation. Developer is also responsible for coordinating with other utilities to resolve conflicts. All costs for these improvements are the applicant's responsibility.'
